passage:
Thursday, 10 pm. I failed the chemistry test. I hid the paper in my bag all afternoon and my stomach hurt through dinner. When Papa asked what was wrong, I burst into tears. I was ready for shouting.
Instead Mummy came round the table and hugged me. Papa started to speak and she said, "Let her breathe first." Then she said, "That must have felt awful." I thought I would feel small, but I felt safe.
So I told them the truth: I skipped revision because I was scared I wouldn't understand it. Mummy and I made a plan for tomorrow evening, one chapter, and I'll explain it back to her. I'll ask Ms. Iqbal to go through the test with me.
Vasudha

qa.q: What did Vasudha expect when she burst into tears, and what did she feel instead?
qa.a: She expected shouting, but she felt safe when Mummy hugged her and said it must have felt awful.

qa.q: What next step did Vasudha and her mother plan?
qa.a: They planned one chapter for tomorrow evening that Vasudha will explain back, and Vasudha will ask Ms. Iqbal to go through the test.

qa.q: What might Mummy have understood about Vasudha's tears?
qa.a: Mummy may have understood that Vasudha was already hurting and scared, so she put comfort first and asked Papa to let Vasudha breathe.

grounding: A parent comforts the teen instead of scolding after a failure, she feels safe, and shares honestly so that they plan the next step together.
